fairness-E.text: '#np' is graded, but the manual (sed.txt:737-742) and instruction.md:6 both say a script whose first two characters are '#n' forces -n. GNU 4.9 forces -n only when '#n' is followed by a newline or end of script, so '#np' keeps autoprint on. The departure is missing from instruction.md:12. Remove these cases or state the newline/end-of-script condition.

addr1,~N where addr1 is already a multiple of N is graded. The manual (sed.txt:1644-1653) literally suggests the range runs to the next multiple, while GNU matches only addr1's line. Clarify in instruction.md or drop the case.

Handling of an empty match right after a previous non-empty match under g (and in Nth-match counting) is not described anywhere; GNU skips it (s/a*/x/g on baaac -> xbxcx), unlike Python re.sub. Specify it or keep such cases out of the grader.

Escaped '|' delimiter inside the regexp under -E (s|a\|b|X| or \|a\|b|p): the manual (sed.txt:4043-4051) only describes the BRE literal reading; GNU drops the backslash, which under ERE may yield alternation. Verify the grader, then specify or exclude the case.

Whether text queued by 'a' is printed when Q runs later in the same cycle is not documented (GNU's Q quits without printing the queue, as I recall). Also unspecified: exit status when a missing file (2) combines with qN. Avoid or specify.
sed.txt:2142 describes \s as spaces, tabs and newlines; GNU uses [[:space:]], which also matches \r, \f and \v. This only matters if replacements put those characters into the pattern space.

The manual only implies that c with '!' (e.g. 2,3!c X) prints the text for every selected line, and does not describe preservation of leading whitespace on a\ continuation text lines; both are reasonable readings.

fairness-F.text: Backslash used as the s command's own delimiter (s\a\b\) is never documented or exemplified in the supplied manual; the correct reading is only reachable by generalizing the documented escaped-delimiter rule to the degenerate case where delimiter and escape character coincide. Consider adding one clarifying sentence to instruction.md, or confirm the graded corpus doesn't probe deeper undocumented behavior here.

addr1,~N when addr1's own line number is already a multiple of N is not directly exemplified; the intended reading (the closing multiple is sought strictly after addr1) requires a short but reasonable inference from the manual's wording.

[.*]-style bracket expressions require combining two separate manual statements (collating-symbol syntax needs a closing sequence; unclosed/mismatched forms fall back to literal-character-in-LIST rules) plus the instruction's exclusion of collating symbols to reach the correct interpretation.

fairness-E.ADDR: overruled: GNU sed 4.9 runs addr1,~N to the next multiple after addr1 (tilde-ends-at-multiple wrong path rejected by the binary-derived expectations); the manual's literal wording, which E read correctly, is the graded behaviour
fairness-E.SCRIPT: overruled: GNU sed 4.9 forces -n for #np (hash-n-needs-newline wrong path rejected); the manual's 'first two characters' rule, which E read correctly, is the graded behaviour
